set.Finding description: Across three independent experiments with excess reelin, axotomy raised surface LRP8 about 2.2-fold in apoE4-treated cultures (~0.45 to ~1.0 surface/total) versus about 1.5-fold in apoE3-treated cultures (~0.62 to ~0.95); the paper calls the apoE3 effect intermediate and shows no apoE4-versus-apoE3 test. This is opposite to lower receptor surface availability with apoE4.

proposal.reason: Quote and n = 3 correct, but ~1.2x matches no apoE3/apoE4 comparison on Fig 4M (after axotomy E4/E3 is ~1.06x; the axotomy response ratio E4 vs E3 is ~2.2/1.5 = ~1.5x). The row's 'greater surface LRP8 response' is the response ratio.
proposal.evidence: Fig 4M (4.png), y axis 0-1.5 surface/total LRP8: Axotomy(-) E3 ~0.62, E4 ~0.45; Axotomy(+) E3 ~0.95, E4 ~1.01. Brackets: E3(-) vs E3(+) p = 0.0092, E4(-) vs E4(+) p < 0.0001; no E3-vs-E4 bracket.

row.Finding description: Across three independent experiments, axotomy left surface LRP8 unchanged without added human apoE but increased it with added apoE4, opposing the predicted loss of surface receptors.
row.Finding quote: With no exogenous human ApoE particles added, axotomy elevated pTyr416 phospho-Src family levels moderately, but did not alter LRP8 distribution. In the presence of added E2, axotomy reduced surface LRP8 and strongly suppressed Src activation. In stark contrast, cultures with E4 showed increased surface LRP8 and Src activation after axotomy.
row.Finding summary: (no added human apoE -> added apoE4) -> (axotomy-associated increase in surface LRP8)
